clue.text: In all cases, those who run a company will be faced with an ordeal

parts.note: a cross to bear is a burden or trial, so an ordeal is a cross
a firm's directors sit together as the board

explanation.surface: Company directors are warned they will all face a gruelling trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will be faced with' is a link: the board has A CROSS in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying to everyone or everything equally is the idiom's sense, matching universally, in every instance.

clue.text: Keyboard instrument — set up authentic start to concert with the inclusion of very small one

indicators.note: the start to a word is its opening letter, here of concert
the reversed word takes the next pieces into its middle, which is what inclusion means
in a down clue, set up means the word is written bottom to top, reading backwards

parts.note: authentic means real
V is short for very, as in the size label VS for very small
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A tiny keyboard instrument is set up at the start of an authentic concert.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' means written upwards, so authentic is turned round; 'with the inclusion of' then wraps it around the very small one, and the concert's opening letter leads.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is any instrument played from a keyboard, such as a harpsichord or clavichord.

clue.text: Make too much of rubbish in old poetry

indicators.note: the rubbish is placed inside the word for poetry

parts.note: poetry is verse
tat is cheap rubbish or junk

explanation.surface: A critic complains of rubbish in old poetry being overrated.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate something is to make more of it than it deserves.

clue.text: Districts to the north installing a despotic ruler?

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the letter a into itself, as if fitting it in
in a down clue, going to the north means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: districts or regions are parts of a country

explanation.surface: Northern districts install an autocratic governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the north' turns PARTS into STRAP, and 'installing' puts A inside it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a provincial governor in ancient Persia, and by extension any petty tyrant.

clue.text: Mistress has poet for socialising primarily

indicators.note: the poet's name stands in for one letter of the word has, taking its place
primarily means taking the first letter of socialising

parts.note: John Milton was the poet of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A kept woman has a poet in tow when she goes out socialising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' signals the swap: MILTON replaces the S (first letter of socialising) in HAS, giving HA + MILTON. Emma Hamilton was Lord Nelson's famous mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma, Lady Hamilton, is history's best-known lover of Admiral Nelson, a famous paramour.

clue.text: Don't admit gangster is tired

parts.note: to ban someone is to refuse them entry
Al Capone is the crossword's stock gangster

explanation.surface: A bouncer is told to keep out a weary gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired here means stale or hackneyed, like a trite, overused remark.

clue.text: A grand time being locked up? Prisoner would rather be this

indicators.note: the letter for time is shut inside the phrase, as a prisoner is in a cell

parts.note: grand means large

explanation.surface: Doing time inside, a prisoner longs for freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being locked up' puts T between A and LARGE; the pun is that the locked-up prisoner wants the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at liberty, free and roaming, is what any inmate wishes to be.

clue.text: An anniversary for which there could be an 'icy' reception?

definitions.text: An anniversary for which there could be an 'icy' reception?

parts.words: An anniversary for which there could be an 'icy' reception?
parts.note: ice is slang for gemstones, so a party marking sixty years of marriage could be called icy, a reception laden with precious stones

explanation.surface: A celebration that might be frosty.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixtieth wedding anniversary is traditionally marked with the hardest gemstone, slangily called ice.

clue.text: Former premier — drunk and a brawler now!

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A one-time prime minister is now a drunken brawler.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Bonar Law was British Prime Minister in 1922-23.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonar Law led the British government briefly in the 1920s, making him an ex-head of government.

clue.text: One not starting an exam with the best-looking desk, say?

indicators.note: the word One loses its opening letter, so it is not starting

parts.note: an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A candidate who doesn't start the exam has the tidiest desk.
explanation.walkthrough: NE (one without its first letter) + A + TEST. A tidy desk, with nothing written on it, is the neatest.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat means tidy, so the tidiest-looking desk belongs to the person who is most orderly.

clue.text: Fellow badly wanting a paper

parts.note: a fellow is a man
ill means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A man in poor health wants a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Manilla is a strong brown wrapping stock, originally made from hemp, used for envelopes.

clue.text: Put back restrictions? Unlikely

parts.note: reins are restraints, as in keeping a tight rein
a tall story is an unlikely tale

explanation.surface: Should the curbs be restored? It seems improbable.
explanation.definitionFit: To fit something again in its former place is to restore or replace it.

clue.text: Very slow ship on lake

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: L is short for lake on maps
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A vessel drifts at a crawl across a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical tempo marking meaning broad and very slow.

clue.text: Conflict witnessed in capital city

parts.note: conflict is war
witnessed means saw

explanation.surface: Fighting is seen in a nation's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Warsaw is the capital of Poland.

clue.text: Nanny may be looked after by me

definitions.text: Nanny may be looked after by me

parts.words: Nanny may be looked after by me
parts.note: a nanny is a female goat, so the speaker is the person tending a flock, not a parent hiring childcare

explanation.surface: A children's nurse is cared for by the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman of goats looks after nannies, the females of the flock.

clue.text: Honest old PM's particular direction

parts.note: honest means true
Lord North was British Prime Minister during the American War of Independence

explanation.surface: An honest former prime minister has his own way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearing towards the geographic pole, as opposed to magnetic, is a specific compass heading.

clue.text: Sort of post mother can get in Nottingham area?

indicators.note: mother is put inside the word for the area, getting in

parts.note: Sherwood Forest lies near Nottingham
ma is mother

explanation.surface: Can a mother find a job in the Nottingham area?
explanation.walkthrough: Sherwood Forest, of Robin Hood fame, is in Nottinghamshire, England. 'Post' is a pole, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A foremast is the mast nearest a ship's bow, a kind of upright spar.

clue.text: Sharp tot, honed to become exceptional

indicators.note: something exceptional is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A bright child is coached to become outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp of time means precisely punctual, as in arriving at six sharp.

clue.text: Stolen property brought back to pub — little pictures etc.lined up

indicators.note: brought back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: loot is stolen goods
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: Thieves bring their haul back to the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer screen, a strip of small icons and buttons arranged in a row is this.

clue.text: He didn't really want an egg the dog munched!

definitions.text: He didn't really want an egg

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
munched means ate

explanation.surface: Someone didn't want their egg, and the dog gobbled it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Punch cartoon, a nervous young clergyman given a bad egg by his bishop says parts of it are excellent; hence a curate's egg, something only partly good.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase curate's egg comes from a junior clergyman politely pretending a stale egg was partly fine.

clue.text: Like a great show in Cornwall starting

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words Cornwall starting

explanation.surface: A grand production is opening in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A show with a cast made entirely of big names is described this way.

clue.text: Dazed state brought by Proust's rambling

indicators.note: rambling suggests wandering about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Reading Proust's long-winded prose leaves one in a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a condition of near-unconsciousness or numbness.

clue.text: Man at 6 frequently up in the air

parts.note: the gangster at 6 down is Al, a man's name
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A man at six o'clock is often airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' points to 6 down, where AL is the gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aloft is high overhead, airborne or raised.

clue.text: Mark's hat being worn by daughter

indicators.note: the hat sits over the daughter, so the letter for daughter goes inside it

parts.note: tile is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Mark's hat is being worn by his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' reads as Mark is; the definition is the accent mark, and Mark is not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy accent over a letter, as in Spanish ñ.

clue.text: Fished with bad net to start with, it being snarled up

indicators.note: the scrambled net comes first, at the start
bad means faulty, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod

explanation.surface: Someone went fishing with a poor net, which got tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' is the anagram signal on net alone; 'to start with' puts that scramble in front of the fishing word, and 'it being' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tangled or knotted is caught up in a snarl.

clue.text: See British essayist producing something flowery

parts.note: lo means see, as in lo and behold
Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: A British essayist produces florid prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Lobelia is a garden plant with small blue or purple blossoms.

clue.text: Train up loony to be a very proper person?

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mad person is being trained up to be prim.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is someone with strict moral standards, prudish or straitlaced.

clue.text: Fantastic cherries — sort we found in English county

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wonderful cherries of the kind found in an English shire.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcestershire is a fruit-growing county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcestershire is a county in the West Midlands region of England.
